property.name: {{PROPERTY_NAME}}
property.neighborhood: Logan Heights / Barrio Logan, San Diego, CA

places.name: Northgate González Market
places.blurb: Full-service Latino supermarket with an excellent produce section, fresh tortillas, and a butcher counter. Great prices and a friendly neighborhood vibe.
places.hostTip: The fresh tortillas from the in-store tortillería are made daily — grab them warm in the morning.

places.name: El Rancho Market
places.blurb: A neighborhood corner market stocked with Mexican staples, snacks, and cold drinks — perfect for a quick grab-and-go.
places.hostTip: Good for basics and late-night snacks when the larger stores are closed.

places.name: Las Cuatro Milpas
places.blurb: A Barrio Logan institution since 1933 — handmade tortillas, slow-cooked beans, and carnitas that draw lines around the block. Cash only, worth every minute.
places.hours: Mon–Fri 8am–3pm, Sat 8am–2pm (cash only, closes when food runs out)
places.hostTip: Arrive before noon or they may run out. Bring cash — no cards accepted.

places.name: Chicano Park Taco Stand
places.blurb: Casual open-air tacos and street food right next to Chicano Park. Simple, authentic, and budget-friendly.
places.hostTip: Great spot to grab lunch after walking through the park murals.

places.name: Coronado Beach
places.blurb: One of the most beautiful beaches in the US — wide white sand, calm surf, and the iconic Hotel del Coronado as a backdrop. Reach it by the Coronado Ferry from downtown.
places.distanceText: 15 min drive or ~30 min via trolley + ferry
places.hostTip: Skip the bridge traffic — take the Broadway Pier ferry from downtown. It drops you right near the beach and the trip itself is scenic.

places.name: Silver Strand State Beach
places.blurb: A quieter, less-crowded stretch of sand on the Coronado peninsula, popular with locals for calm water and wide open space.
places.hostTip: Less crowded than Coronado Beach on weekends. Bring cash or a card for the parking kiosk.

places.name: Chicano Park
places.blurb: A National Historic Landmark with one of the largest collections of outdoor murals in the US. The murals cover the freeway pylons with vivid Chicano history and art — a genuinely moving place to walk through.
places.hostTip: The murals on the underside of the Coronado Bridge pylons are the heart of it — walk the full perimeter for the complete experience.

places.name: Barrio Logan Arts District
places.blurb: The neighborhood surrounding the property is a hub of galleries, studios, and street art. A self-guided walk along Logan Ave and National Ave reveals rotating murals and small galleries.
places.address: Logan Ave & National Ave, San Diego, CA 92113
places.hours: Galleries typically Fri–Sun 11am–5pm; street art always accessible
places.hostTip: Check if it's the third Saturday of the month — several studios open for a community art walk.

places.name: Barrio Logan Trolley Station (Blue Line)
places.blurb: The Blue Line trolley runs from here to downtown San Diego in about 10 minutes, and continues south to the US–Mexico border. Reliable, cheap, and no parking stress.
places.hours: Approx. 5am–midnight daily; check MTS for current schedule
places.hostTip: A day pass covers unlimited rides — good value if you're doing downtown + Coronado Ferry in one day. Buy on the platform ticket machine or the MTS app.

places.name: Airport (SAN) Access
places.blurb: San Diego International Airport is just 10–15 minutes away by car. By trolley take the Blue Line to downtown, then the 992 bus to the airport — about 30 minutes total.
places.distanceText: 10 min drive / 30 min by trolley + bus
places.address: 3225 N Harbor Dr, San Diego, CA 92101
places.hostTip: Rideshare (Uber/Lyft) from the property is usually under $15. Pickup from the app lot is on the north side of the terminal.
